dedupe_keys.name: agricultural conservation planning framework acpf database field boundaries crop rotations and soils

description: The ACPF database gives soils and land use data for small agricultural watersheds, built to be used with the Agricultural Conservation Planning Framework toolkit that identifies conservation practices to cut nutrient discharge. The DataCite record from USDA Agricultural Research Service says soil data were extracted from the NRCS Web Soil Survey, and agricultural field polygons were edited from a public USDA field boundary dataset (pre-2008) with ownership removed, checked against the 2009 Cropland Data Layer and NAIP aerial photography, then each field was classed by its 2007 to 2012 crop sequence into major rotations, mostly corn and soybean. It was issued in 2015 by D.E. James on Ag Data Commons, free to download; the licence, file formats and the list of watersheds covered are not stated on the pages read. Coverage is US agricultural watersheds, dominated by the corn and soybean belt. Caveats: the page says LiDAR elevation models are needed by the toolkit but are not included, and land use reflects 2007 to 2012. For simulation it gives field-level land use and rotations to model nutrient runoff, drainage and conservation practice placement, and field polygons for agricultural exposure in flood scenarios. Related catalogue records include the USGS subsurface tile drainage extent estimates and the Crop Map of England (CROME).
